newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold, platinum futures end lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold, platinum futures end lower.

text.p: Tokyo gold and platinum futures ended lower on Friday, pressured by weaker spot metal prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to six yen per gram lower. Benchmark August ended four yen down at 1,337 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from three to 10 yen per gram lower with benchmark August finishing down six yen at 1,372 yen.

Spot gold prices eased slightly in reaction to a report in the New York Times that the IMF has said that it might sell some of its $40 billion holdings of gold to reduce the debts of the poorest countries.
Spot gold was quoted at $387.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $387.60/388.10 in New York on Thursday.

"After the news, spot gold prices edged down gradually, pressured by selling by Swiss banks, but further price losses are likely to be limited by good physical gold demand in Asia," an senior dealer at a foreign bank said.
In the gold futures market, mixed trade by commodity brokers was noted on Friday.
Platinum futures extended losses in the afternoon session on selling by trade houses. Activity was dominated by spread-trade by trading houses, they said.
One trader said the sharp losses in Japan's stock market undermined sentiment in Japan's platinum futures market.
The Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei average tumbled nearly two percent on Friday, extending its losses for a third straight day.
Palladium futures ended mostly firmer on technical buying. Prices ranged from one yen per gram lower to four yen firmer. Benchmark August finished three yen firmer at 441 yen.
Silver futures were mixed, with prices ranging from 1.0 yen per 10 grams lower to 0.3 yen firmer. Benchmark August finished 1.0 yen down at 182.7 yen.
